OC2 = OE2 + EC2

OC2 = 122 + 352

OC = 37 cm

BC = 37 + 12 = 49

Let AB = AE = 'a' cm

In ∆ABC-

AC2 = AB2 + BC2

(a + 35)2 = a2 + 492

a2 + 1225 + 70a = a2 + 2401

a = 16.8 cm

questions.q_en: Find the length of the common chord of two circles having radii equal to 60 cm and 50 cm whose centres are 50 cm apart.
questions.solution_en:
Let 'O' and 'P' be the centres of the circle having radii equal to 60 cm and 50 cm, respectively

Therefore, OP is the line joining the centres of the two circle

According to the question,

OP = 50 cm

Let length of OA be 'x' cm.

Therefore, AP = (50 - x) cm

From ΔMOA, using Pythagoras theorem

MA2 = (602 - x2)

In ΔMPA

MA2 = 502 - (50 - x)2

Therefore, MA2 = (602 - x2) = 502 - (50 - x)2

Or, 3600 - x2 = 2500 - 2500 - x2 + 100x

Or, 3600 = 100x

So, 'x' = 36

So, MA2 = 602 - 362

Or, MA2 = 3600 - 1296

Or, MA2 = 2304

So, MA = 48 (Since, length cannot be negative therefore, we will take the positive root only)

So, MN = 2 X MA = 2 X 48 = 96 cm

questions.q_en: The radius of two circles with centres X and Y are 12 cm and 6 cm, respectively. If a transverse common tangent MN to both the circles which cuts the line joining the both centres X and Y at point O such that MO = 16 cm, then what is the distance between both centres of the circles if M is point on bigger circle and N is point on smaller circle?
questions.solution_en:
MO = 16 cm

Since ∠XMO = ∠ONY = 90°

By Pythagoras theorem,

XO2 = XM2 + MO2

=> XO2 = 122 + 162

=> XO2 = 144 + 256 = 400

=> XO = 20 cm

Since ∠XMO = ∠ONY = 90°

And ∠MOX = ∠YON (transverse angle)

So, ∠MXO = ∠OYN

Hence, ∆XMO and ∆OYN are similar triangles.

XM/YN = XO/YO

=> 12/6 = 20/YO

=> YO = 20/2 = 10 cm

Hence, XY = XO + OY = 20 + 10 = 30 cm

questions.solution_en:
Since, two tangents from same point are always equal.

Thus, MB = BA = 18.9 cm, and AB = BN = 18.9 cm

questions.solution_en:
Radius of circle = 9 cm

Therefore, OA = OB = 9 cm

From point P, PA and PB are two tangents at A and B are drawn, therefore PA = PB = Y (Let)

Perimeter of quadrilateral = 40 cm

PA + AO + OB + PB = 40

Y + 9 + 9 + Y = 40

2Y = 22

Y = 11

Therefore, the value of (PA - OA) = 11 - 9 = 2 cm.

questions.q_en: A tangent XY touches a circle at A. Two chords are drawn from A to B and C such that BC = BA. If angle made by chord AB with tangent XY is 75⁰ respectively, and D is a point on minor arc of BC, then find ∠BDC.
questions.solution_en:
XY is the tangent that touches the circle at A.

∠YAB = ∠ACB = 75⁰ (property of circle)

Since, BC = BA;

∠ACB = ∠CAB = 75⁰

Hence, ∠CAB + ∠BDC = 180⁰ (sum of angles on opposite arcs)

∠BDC = 180⁰ - 75⁰ = 105⁰

questions.q_en: A circle is inscribed in a quadrilateral STUV. If the length of sides ST, TU, and UV are 21.4 cm, 18.6 cm, and 24.8 cm, respectively, then what is the length of the side VS?
questions.solution_en:
We know that,

When a circle touches all the four sides of a quadrilateral STUV, then

ST + UV = TU + VS

=> (21.4 + 24.8) = (18.6 + VS)

=> VS = 46.2 - 18.6

=> VS = 27.6 cm

questions.q_en: In following diagram length of chords PQ and RS are 10cm and 8cm respectively and total length of MN is 9cm which passes through centre C of the given circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution_en:
Let r be the radius of circle and length of CM = x cm.

Length of CN = (9-x) cm. Perpendicular to any chord from the centre of

circle bisect it.

(r)2 = (x)2 + (4)2

(r)2= (x)2 + 16 ----------(1)

Similarly

(r)2= (9 - x) 2 + (5) 2

(r) 2 = (9 - x) 2 + 25 ----------(2)

From equations (1) and (2) we get

(x)2+ 16 = (9 - x) 2 + 25

x² = 81-18x +x² + 9

18x = 90

x = 5 cm

r2 = 25 + 16 = 41

r= √41 cm

questions.q_en: Find the length of chord MP if MQ is diameter of length 16 cm and ∠MNO = 45°.
questions.solution_en:
∠MPQ = 90° (MQ is the diameter and any triangle inscribed in a semicircle is always a right angle.)

∠PQO + ∠PNO = 180°(PNOQ is a cyclic quadrilateral.)

∠PQO = 180° - 45° = 135°

∠PQM = 180° - 135° = 45°

In △MPQ, ∠PMQ = 180° - 90° - 45° = 45°

So, MP = PQ (Let them be 'x')

MQ2 = MP2 + PQ2

162 = x2 + x2

2x2 = 256

x2 = 128

MP = x = 8√2 cm

questions.q_en: From a point P outside the circle of center O, a tangent PT of length 12√3 cm is drawn. PBA is secant, radius of circle is 13 cm and perpendicular distance of chord AB from the center is 5 cm, then find the length of PA (PA > PB).
questions.solution_en:
PT = 12√3 cm

AO = 13 cm

OM = 5 cm

AM = √(AO2 - OM2) = √(132 - 52) = 12 cm

AB = 24 cm

We know that: PT2 = PA * PB

Let PB = 'x' cm

(12√3)2 = (x + 24) * x

x2 + 24x = 432

x2 + 24x - 432 = 0

x = 12

PA = x + 24 = 36 cm

questions.q_en: In the figure given below, DC (= 2√85 cm) is the diameter of the circle, BE = 2 cm and BC = 12 cm. If AD = 6 cm, then calculate the value of AE.
questions.solution_en:
Here, ∠A = ∠B = 90˚ (because if one side of a triangle inscribed in a circle is equal to diameter of the circle, then the triangle formed is a right angled triangle.)

Then, by using Pythagoras theorem:

DC2 = BD2 + BC2

(2√85)2 = BD2 + 122

BD = 14 cm

Now, DE = BD - BE = 14 - 2 = 12 cm

Similarly, DE2 = AD2 + AE2

122 = 62 + AE2

AE = 6√3 cm

questions.q_en: A circle of centre O circumscribed a triangle PQR and a tangent MQ is drawn at point Q. It is also given that- ∠PRQ = 70°, ∠PQM = x° and ∠OPQ = y°, then what is the value of (x - y)?
questions.solution_en:
∠PRQ = 70°, ∠PQM = x° and ∠OPQ = y°

∠OQP = ∠OPQ [OP = OQ = Radius]

∠POQ = 2 * ∠PRQ [Angle which is subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the size of the angle subtended at any point on the circumference]

∠POQ = 2 * 70° = 140°

In △POQ-

∠POQ + ∠OQP + ∠OPQ = 180°

140° + ∠OPQ + ∠OPQ = 180°

∠OPQ = y° = 20°

y = 20

∠OQM = 90° [Angle between radius and tangent.]

∠OQP + ∠PQM = 90°

x° = 90° - 20°

x = 70

(x - y) = 70 - 20 = 50°

questions.q_en: In the given figure, O is the center and KOL is a diameter of the circle. If ∠ KOM = 140° then ∠ LMN =?
questions.solution_en:
Given,

∠ KOM = 140°

So,

∠ KLM = 140/2 = 70° [angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on circumference]

Now,

OL = OM = Radius

So, ∠ OLM = ∠ OML = 70°

We know that angle between the tangent and radius at point of contact = 90°

So, ∠ OMN = 90°

Therefore,

∠ LMN = ∠ OMN - ∠ OML = 90 - 70 = 20°

questions.q_en: There is a circle with centre B and AD and AC are two tangents to the circle such that ∠DAB = 30°. If radius of the circle is 18 cm, then what is the value of √3(AD + AC)?
questions.solution_en:
∠DAB = ∠CAB = 30°

In ∆ABC,

tan 30° = CB/AC

=> 1/√3 = 18/AC

=> AC = 18√3 cm = AD

Hence, √3(AD + AC) = √3 * 2 * 18√3 = 108
